summary: The tools component is the act stage of the loop. A ToolRegistry holds every Tool (each implementing name/description/schema/execute plus is_readonly/is_destructive/risk_level metadata) as critical (always active) or deferred (discovered via tool_search). The agent collects CollectedToolCalls from the LLM, partitions them into parallel-safe read-only and sequential mutating batches, gates each through safety/cache/schema checks, executes tool.execute, and feeds JSON ToolResults back as tool-role messages.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/tools/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in the Tool trait, ToolRegistry register_critical/register_deferred/activate, tool_search.rs, and the agent tool_dispatch execute_tool_batch / execute_single_tool path.

examples.title: Register critical tools as always-on act nodes
examples.intent: Guarantee core file and shell tools are executable from turn one without discovery.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolRegistry::register_critical activates a Tool immediately and includes it in critical_definitions, so the act stage always has file_read/file_write/shell_exec/grep_search available.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User drags a critical tool node from the palette into the always-on shelf that stays pinned to the act stage.
touch_interaction.visual: Critical tool nodes render solid and pinned with a small anchor icon; they never dim.

examples.mini_scenario: On startup the registry pre-registers file and shell tools as critical, and the first Executing turn can call them directly.
examples.pitfall: Registering too many tools as critical bloats the tool list and eats the context budget on every turn.

examples.title: Defer niche tools behind tool_search
examples.intent: Keep rarely-used tools out of the prompt until the loop actually needs them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: register_deferred adds a Tool to the graph without activating it; it is absent from definitions until tool_search discovers it and activate flips it on, shrinking per-turn context.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the tool_search hub fans out the deferred tools as ghosted nodes waiting to be summoned.
touch_interaction.visual: Deferred nodes render translucent; on activation they snap to full opacity with a pop.

examples.mini_scenario: The model calls tool_search('git status'), the registry returns git_status, and a later turn activates and runs it.
examples.pitfall: Marking a genuinely core tool deferred forces an extra discovery round-trip that wastes a turn.

examples.title: Discover a tool via the search index
examples.intent: Let the model find the right tool by intent rather than memorizing the full catalog.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolSearchTool::execute queries the shared index and returns ToolSearchResults (name, description, schema, category); the model then acts on a discovered tool in the next turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the search node opens a query field; results appear as candidate nodes the user can drag onto the canvas.
touch_interaction.visual: Matching candidates glow by relevance; the top match pulses brightest.

examples.mini_scenario: A task needs container control; the model searches 'run container', gets container_run, and calls it next turn.
examples.pitfall: Returning too many low-relevance matches floods the context and dilutes the model's tool choice.

examples.title: Partition into a parallel-safe read batch
examples.intent: Run independent read-only tools concurrently to save wall-clock time.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: execute_tool_batch uses is_parallel_safe (backed by is_readonly metadata) to split reads with no path conflicts into a parallel batch, collapsing many act turns into one concurrent burst.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User spreads fingers over a group of read nodes to fan them into parallel lanes that execute side by side.
touch_interaction.visual: Parallel read nodes light green simultaneously and their edges animate in lockstep.

examples.mini_scenario: Three grep_search calls on different paths run in one parallel batch and their results return together.
examples.pitfall: Treating a non-read-only tool as parallel-safe risks interleaved writes and nondeterministic state.

examples.title: Serialize mutating tools
examples.intent: Prevent overlapping writes from racing on shared files.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The dispatch partition routes mutating tools (file_write, patch_apply, shell_exec) and path-conflicting operations into a sequential batch executed one at a time, serializing state changes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a single-file chain connecting mutating nodes so they line up on one execution track.
touch_interaction.visual: Mutating nodes render amber and queue in a visible single-lane conveyor.

examples.mini_scenario: Two file_edit calls on the same file are forced sequential so the second sees the first's result.
examples.pitfall: Parallelizing two edits to the same path can clobber one change and produce a corrupt file.

examples.title: Gate a call through the safety checker
examples.intent: Deny or prompt on dangerous tool calls before they execute.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: execute_single_tool applies safety.check_tool_call, which can deny or require confirmation based on ExecutionMode, so the act stage is guarded rather than trusting the LLM blindly.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a tool node opens its safety gate panel showing risk level and the current mode's policy.
touch_interaction.visual: High-risk nodes wear a red shield badge; the shield glows when a confirmation is pending.

examples.mini_scenario: A shell_exec of 'rm -rf' is flagged high-risk; in Normal mode the gate prompts before the tool runs.
examples.pitfall: Skipping the safety gate in an autonomous mode lets a destructive command execute with no checkpoint.

examples.title: Validate args against the tool schema
examples.intent: Reject malformed tool calls before they reach execute.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: validate_tool_call checks the parsed args against the Tool's JSON schema; a mismatch produces a synthetic error ToolResult so the model corrects itself instead of the tool crashing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a tool node flips it to show its schema slots; missing required fields highlight before execution.
touch_interaction.visual: Unfilled required slots glow red; a valid call turns the node border green.

examples.mini_scenario: The model omits the required 'path' arg for file_read; schema validation returns an error the model fixes next turn.
examples.pitfall: Bypassing schema validation pushes bad args into execute and surfaces an opaque runtime error instead of a fixable one.

examples.title: Serve a cached read result
examples.intent: Avoid re-running an identical read-only tool call.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_cacheable identifies read-only tools; the ToolCache keyed on tool_name+args returns a hit, so the act stage skips execution entirely and saves budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a read node shows a cache badge; a hit routes the edge straight to the cached result card.
touch_interaction.visual: A cache hit renders a lightning bolt badge and the node skips its spin animation.

examples.mini_scenario: A repeated grep_search with identical args returns instantly from the ToolCache with no re-execution.
examples.pitfall: Caching a tool whose file changed under it (no mtime check) serves stale evidence to the loop.

examples.title: Invalidate cache after a mutation
examples.intent: Keep the read cache honest once files change.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After a mutating tool, invalidate_path clears entries for the touched path (and shell_exec clears the whole cache), so subsequent reads re-execute against fresh state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks a write node's output edge across the cache to sweep away stale entries for that path.
touch_interaction.visual: Invalidated cache cards shatter and fade; affected read nodes lose their lightning badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A file_write invalidates that path's cache so the next file_read reflects the new content.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting to invalidate after shell_exec's arbitrary side effects leaves the whole cache stale.

examples.title: Return a ToolResult as a tool-role message
examples.intent: Feed execution output back into the conversation for the next reason turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: execute_single_tool returns (success, result_json, summary); the JSON is pushed as a tool-role Message so the LLM perceives the outcome and reasons about the next act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws an edge from the tool node back to the reason node to route its result into the next turn.
touch_interaction.visual: Success results flow along a green edge; failures flow along a red edge carrying the error summary.

examples.mini_scenario: cargo_test returns JSON with pass/fail; that becomes a tool message and the model reasons over the failures.
examples.pitfall: Dropping the tool_call_id on the result message breaks the LLM's pairing of call to output.

examples.title: Attach a vision result as evidence
examples.intent: Feed image output into a verification turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: For vision tools the ToolResult carries base64_png plus an image_attached marker in the summary, so the verify stage can reason over a screenshot instead of text alone.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading a vision node enlarges its result into a thumbnail preview of the captured image.
touch_interaction.visual: The node grows an image chip with a camera badge; it pulses once when the capture lands.

examples.mini_scenario: screen_capture returns a PNG; the verify turn inspects the rendered UI to confirm the change is visible.
examples.pitfall: Emitting the raw base64 into the text log instead of the image slot bloats context and hides the picture.

examples.title: Suppress a repeated failed call
examples.intent: Stop the loop from re-running a call that already failed the same way.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: suppress_repeated_failed_tool_retry blocks a tool+args combination that previously failed, returning a synthetic result that nudges the model to change approach rather than re-thrash.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a tool node shows its failure history; a repeat is greyed out with a 'blocked' stamp.
touch_interaction.visual: A repeated failed node dims and wears a red no-entry badge instead of running.

examples.mini_scenario: The model retries file_read on a nonexistent path; the guard blocks the third identical attempt and suggests a fix.
examples.pitfall: Suppressing a call that would now succeed (state changed since the failure) blocks legitimate progress.

examples.title: Block a redundant re-read
examples.intent: Stop the model from reading the same unchanged file over and over.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: maybe_block_redundant_reread blocks re-reading the same file unchanged more than a few times, returning a hint so the loop spends budget on action instead of re-perceiving.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a read node shows a re-read counter; crossing the limit stamps it blocked.
touch_interaction.visual: The counter ticks up and turns red at the limit, then the node shows a loop-block icon.

examples.mini_scenario: After three identical file_reads of an unchanged file, the guard blocks the fourth and tells the model to proceed.
examples.pitfall: Blocking a re-read after the file legitimately changed hides real new content from the loop.

examples.title: Enforce task tool-policy allow/deny
examples.intent: Honor explicit allow/disallow tool lists carried in the task instructions.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: current_task_tool_policy_violation checks a call against the task's allow/deny lists and blocks disallowed tools, scoping the act stage to what the task authorized.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the act hub reveals the allow/deny collar; disallowed tools sit outside the permitted ring.
touch_interaction.visual: Allowed tools glow inside a green ring; denied tools sit greyed beyond a red boundary.

examples.mini_scenario: A task disallows network tools; a http_request call is blocked by the policy before it can execute.
examples.pitfall: Applying a stale policy from a previous task can wrongly block tools the current task actually needs.

examples.title: Bound execution with a concurrency permit
examples.intent: Cap how many tools run at once so the host is not overwhelmed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: execute_single_tool_inner acquires a concurrency governor permit before calling run_tool_bounded, throttling the parallel fanout to configured limits.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the act hub reveals a permit dial showing active vs. maximum concurrent tools.
touch_interaction.visual: The dial fills as permits are taken; waiting nodes shimmer until a permit frees up.

examples.mini_scenario: Ten read tools are queued but only max_tools run concurrently; the rest wait for a permit.
examples.pitfall: Setting the permit ceiling too high can exhaust file handles or subprocess slots on the host.

examples.title: Fire PreToolUse hooks before execute
examples.intent: Let external hooks inspect or veto a tool call before it runs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The act path fires PreToolUse hooks; a HookAction::Skip response short-circuits execution, turning tools into a hookable substrate rather than a hard-coded path.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a hook edge tapping into a tool node's input so the hook fires before execution.
touch_interaction.visual: A hook tap glows on the edge and blinks when it fires; a Skip response reddens the tool node.

examples.mini_scenario: A PreToolUse hook rejects a shell_exec by returning Skip, and the loop proceeds without running it.
examples.pitfall: A slow or hanging hook stalls the entire act stage since execution waits on the hook result.

examples.title: Log every tool call to the audit trail
examples.intent: Make every act observable and replayable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: log_tool_call records name, args, result, success, and duration; the audit JSONL captures the full act history for the checkpoint and post-hoc analysis.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a tool node opens its call log with timings and success flags.
touch_interaction.visual: Each executed node stamps a small ledger badge; failures show a red mark in the log strip.

examples.mini_scenario: Every tool call appends a ToolCallLog entry so the run can be audited and replayed later.
examples.pitfall: Logging raw secrets in tool args leaks credentials into the audit trail; redact before writing.

examples.title: Distinguish readonly from destructive metadata
examples.intent: Let the loop reason about a tool's blast radius before choosing it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Tool::is_readonly/is_destructive/risk_level (from default_tool_metadata) let the dispatch and safety layers decide parallelizability and gating, shaping which tools run when.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a tool node reveals its metadata badges for read-only, destructive, and risk level.
touch_interaction.visual: Read-only nodes show a blue eye; destructive nodes show a red flame; risk shows a 1-3 dot meter.

examples.mini_scenario: file_read is tagged read-only so it joins the parallel batch, while file_delete is destructive and gated.
examples.pitfall: Mislabeling a mutating tool as read-only lets it into the parallel batch and races other writes.

examples.title: Rebuild the search index after registration
examples.intent: Keep tool discovery accurate after tools are added at runtime.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: rebuild_search_index repopulates the shared ToolSearchResult index (behind an RwLock) so newly registered deferred tools become discoverable via tool_search.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks the search hub to refresh its candidate pool, pulling in any newly added tools.
touch_interaction.visual: The index shimmers and new candidate nodes fade into the discoverable pool.

examples.mini_scenario: An MCP server registers a new tool; rebuild_search_index makes it findable so the model can discover and call it.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting to rebuild after late registration hides new tools from tool_search entirely.

examples.title: Slim the prompt with critical-only definitions
examples.intent: Send only the tools the loop actually needs each turn to protect the budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: critical_definitions returns schemas for only critical tools, shrinking the per-turn tool list; deferred tools reach the prompt solely after activation, keeping the reason turn lean.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the tool shelf collapses deferred tools out of view, leaving only critical nodes on the act rail.
touch_interaction.visual: Deferred nodes fold away with a token-saved badge; only pinned critical nodes remain visible.

examples.mini_scenario: The request carries only critical tool definitions, so the model sees a short focused toolset and saves context.
examples.pitfall: Sending the full definitions() every turn wastes thousands of tokens on tools the model will never call.
